verdict.rationale: First-party self-hosting docs say Supermemory runs on your own hardware as a single self-contained binary, with a local graph engine, local embeddings and a local LLM, so data never leaves the building. That satisfies the 'against local models, no cloud dependency' branch of the story. All of this is vendor-claimed only. missing for 10: an embedded in-process library mode (only a standalone binary is documented), details on which local models are supported and how to configure them, and independent or hands-on corroboration of fully offline operation.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run the memory layer fully locally — embedded in-process or against local models — without any cloud dependency

citations.quote: Local graph engine, local embeddings, local LLM. Your data never leaves the building.
Supermemory runs on your own hardware. It's the same memory engine behind the hosted platform... as a single self-contained binary.
No Docker. No database to provision. No config files. It boots in seconds with everything built in
State-of-the-art memory, running on your machine. One binary, zero config.
